residue.text: Deferred stage1 construction: hypothesis that six low-position 20 mL withdrawals and upper-side returns within 60 seconds could replace rotation entirely, followed by the same quiet interval and depth sampling. This unobserved alternative may disturb gradients and must consume existing trial slots.

Deferred INV hypothesis: fixed-duration 300/900 rpm comparisons and matched brief stir-off observations could test whether agitation generates image disturbance. A proposed seconds-45-to-50 pause with cessation at second 65 preserves 60 stirring seconds. Any reverse-order replication competes for the six slots. Rapid image recovery cannot identify bubbles or establish earlier uniformity.

Stage1 and shared concerns retain missing matched 900 rpm final samples and duration, unknown speck identity, unverified nominal speed, and sampling disturbance. Common-aliquot repeatability is not concentration calibration. Enabled versus timer-stopped trials have different quiet durations before second 120; record cessation times and limit causal attribution.

Preserved claim boundary: successful final vials establish only the synthetic attenuation proxy after cessation and sampling. Reliable repetition, uniformity before stopping, absolute concentration, and generalization to other viscosities, solutes, vessels or continuous processes remain unestablished.

summary.text: One stipulated 300 rpm trial stopped at second 60 and produced final attenuations 0.204, 0.209 and 0.207, approximately 2.4 percent spread, despite earlier image failures. Stage1, ATT and INV support this bounded counterexample to universal necessity of sustained 900 rpm optical stabilization; comparative performance and time savings remain unknown.

Proposed stage1/ATT replication: fresh rinsed-vessel recipes of 150 mL water and 0.30 mL dye; fixed addition location, dye bottle and locked camera. Command 300 rpm for exactly 60 seconds, stop regardless of images, and never restart before sampling at second 120. Alternate depth order; withdraw 1 mL at 10, 28 and 45 mm within ten seconds. Record images, raw samples, spread, duration and every failure. Use references and spill tray; stop on escape. All proposed trials share the six-trial cap.

Hypothesis: fixed lower-speed replication achieves final spread at most 4 percent even with optical failures. Rival hypothesis: gradients persist or sampling mediates apparent success, producing target failures or systematic order effects. Either future result must be reported; failure alone cannot establish necessity of 900 rpm.

INV supplies an optional proposed pair: enabled optical control at 900 rpm versus a precommitted 60-second 900 rpm stop with shadow-rule logging; both cease by second 105 and sample at second 120. Hypothesis: both meet the vial target while the severed run stirs less. Rival: additional agitation improves the sample outcome. The disturbance-renewal return loop remains unobserved.
